I ported the program to Rust and it passes all 6 example cases in `node check.mjs`. On two 50 MB inputs, one of generated words and one of random bytes, its output was byte-for-byte the same as the Python original's, and each run took about 0.15 s.

The code is in `src/main.rs` and uses only the standard library. It lowercases the input in place, counts words without copying each one, and then picks out the top 10. It also includes 4 unit tests, which pass.

`build.sh` builds the optimized binar
